output_parsed.paper_title: Spirit Mars Rover Mission to the Columbia Hills, Gusev Crater: Mission overview and selected results from the Cumberland Ridge to Home Plate

queries.query: For MER Spirit in Gusev Crater (Columbia Hills, Husband Hill), I need the Pancam multispectral reduced-data panorama from sol ~549 to quantify bedding geometry and clast/matrix textural variability in the layered outcrops at the Voltaire locality for stratigraphic interpretation.

For MER Spirit Pancam multispectral (0.4–1.0 µm) observations in the Columbia Hills during the Low Ridge winter-campaign season (around sol ~1070), I need a reduced-data product suitable for deriving reflectance trends of a vesicular basalt boulder and comparing those spectral characteristics against dust- and hematite-influenced materials in the Inner Basin.

queries.query: I need calibrated Mini-TES thermal-infrared radiance spectra (5–29 µm) acquired by the Spirit Mars Exploration Rover in Gusev Crater during the Columbia Hills traverse (including the Husband Hill outcrop campaign and subsequent Inner Basin/Low Ridge operations, roughly mid-mission sols) to build and compare spectral end-members for altered outcrops versus basaltic sands.

I need summed Mössbauer backscatter spectra from Spirit in Gusev Crater across Columbia Hills targets (outcrops on Husband Hill plus key ripple-field and hematite-rich platy outcrops near Home Plate, spanning the main Columbia Hills campaigns) to quantify Fe-bearing mineral modes and oxidation state (Fe3+/Fetotal) for aqueous-alteration interpretation.

final_output.query: Locate the Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter CRISM full‑resolution targeted hyperspectral observation over the Columbia Hills in Gusev crater acquired during the Spirit Low Ridge winter campaign, using the empirically corrected targeted product to quantify 0.4–4.0 µm endmember mixing (dust vs. olivine/pyroxene) at ~18 m/pixel across Husband Hill, Tennessee Valley, and the El Dorado ripple field.

Identify the PDS archive dataset that contains the Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter CRISM raw experiment data records for Mars hyperspectral observations (0.4–4.0 µm) so I can run my own DISORT-based atmospheric correction and retrieve surface Lambert albedo spectra for regional analyses such as Gusev crater/Columbia Hills at full‑resolution targeted scale.

Assemble Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter Context Camera panchromatic imagery at ~6 m/pixel over Gusev Crater, emphasizing coverage of the Columbia Hills and adjacent cratered plains, to generate a geologic context basemap suitable for sharpening and co-registering with orbital hyperspectral products.

Retrieve the Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter Context Camera instrument reference metadata (e.g., spectral bandpass, optics/detector characteristics, and stated spatial resolution) required to interpret panchromatic image intensity and evaluate CTX suitability for contextual mapping of the Columbia Hills region.

Locate the Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter HiRISE red-band reduced-data image that covers the Columbia Hills portion of Gusev Crater (including the Husband Hill to Inner Basin/Home Plate traverse corridor) so I can use it as a high-resolution geomorphic basemap for rover traverse and experiment-site overlay mapping.

Identify the Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter HiRISE Reduced Data Record (RDR) archive release (version 1.1) needed for consistent, map-projected high-resolution imaging inputs when building regional basemaps and mosaics for Mars surface operations and geologic context mapping in areas like Gusev Crater.

For MER Spirit in Gusev Crater (Columbia Hills, Husband Hill), I need the Pancam multispectral reduced-data panorama from sol ~549 to quantify bedding geometry and clast/matrix textural variability in the layered outcrops at the Voltaire locality for stratigraphic interpretation.

For MER Spirit Pancam multispectral (0.4–1.0 µm) observations in the Columbia Hills during the Low Ridge winter-campaign season (around sol ~1070), I need a reduced-data product suitable for deriving reflectance trends of a vesicular basalt boulder and comparing those spectral characteristics against dust- and hematite-influenced materials in the Inner Basin.

I need calibrated Mini-TES thermal-infrared radiance spectra (5–29 µm) acquired by the Spirit Mars Exploration Rover in Gusev Crater during the Columbia Hills traverse (including the Husband Hill outcrop campaign and subsequent Inner Basin/Low Ridge operations, roughly mid-mission sols) to build and compare spectral end-members for altered outcrops versus basaltic sands.

I need summed Mössbauer backscatter spectra from Spirit in Gusev Crater across Columbia Hills targets (outcrops on Husband Hill plus key ripple-field and hematite-rich platy outcrops near Home Plate, spanning the main Columbia Hills campaigns) to quantify Fe-bearing mineral modes and oxidation state (Fe3+/Fetotal) for aqueous-alteration interpretation.
